newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rates end down as speculation fades.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rates end down as speculation fades.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rates reversed earlier gains to close down 17 basis points at 29.33 percent on Tuesday after early speculation abated, traders said.
"Overnight rates were under great upside pressure this morning. There was a sort of fight against one big intermediary that was trying to force rates up," said a trader.
"Rates eased off towards the close, albeit on thin volume," he added.
Overnight rates reached a high of 29.75 percent during the session.
Other traders said that early pressure on rates was due to slight early weakness in the peso, and that rates thus recovered along with the peso in late trade.
The 48-hour peso earlier closed 1.1 centavos softer at 7.9050/7.9100 per dollar, but had been 2.6 centavos off at one stage.
Traders said they expected short-term Cetes rates to gain at this evening's Banco de Mexico auction, despite relative stability in the foreign exchange market.
The reason for this was that inflation normally reaches a seasonal spike in November and December, and rates thus need to gain in order to preserve expected real returns.
A Reuters survey of ten Cetes dealers showed they expected the bellwether 27-day rate rising 21 basis points to 29.66 percent at the primary auction.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed down 60 basis points at 30.50 percent.
Banco de Mexico injected 4.719 billion pesos by auctioning four credits, which it assigned at between 31.17 percent and 31.89 percent.
Traders said that liquidity shortages resulting from credit maturities of 8.509 billion pesos were eased by government spending of some 2.7 billion pesos.
Total credit maturities for Wednesday were estimated at 3.769 billion pesos.
